items.title: Market Liquidations Triggered by Inflation Shock
points: Nearly $1 billion in crypto positions liquidated on October 15 as Bitcoin fell below $80,000 for the first time in over a month following hotter-than-expected inflation data that revived Fed rate-hike expectations.
90% of liquidated positions were long (bullish) bets, meaning leveraged traders betting on price increases bore the brunt of the selloff.
High-beta assets (volatile securities that amplify broader market movements) saw the biggest losses as investors reduced risk exposure ahead of potential Fed rate hikes.

items.title: Altcoins Face Macro Pressure
points: Ethereum (ETH), Ripple (XRP), and Solana (SOL) all declined significantly as altcoins suffered outsized drawdowns from macroeconomic pressures.
Zcash (ZEC), a privacy-focused cryptocurrency, tanked double digits as leverage built up during its recent rally unwound, though it remains up several hundred percent from its March lows.

items.title: AI Threat to Crypto Signatures
points: Ethereum Foundation researcher Justin Drake warned that AI could crack ECDSA signatures (the cryptographic method securing private keys and transaction authenticity) before quantum computers pose a threat, urging the industry to prepare.

items.title: Ledger Launches New Hardware Wallet
points: Ledger announced an Android-based 'Atom' touchscreen hardware wallet with anti-tamper protections, sold only through official channels.
Launch follows investigations into tampered resold devices in the secondary market.

items.title: Crypto Scam Takedown
points: Brooklyn prosecutors shut down 112 servers behind a crypto scam targeting Russian-speaking victims.
The operation also ran a fake recovery service that contacted victims weeks later with false promises to recover stolen assets.

items.title: Morgan Stanley's Digital Gold Framework
points: Morgan Stanley released research positioning bitcoin as 'digital gold,' comparing it to traditional gold as a store of value and inflation hedge.
The bank framed bitcoin as a portfolio allocation option for institutional investors seeking non-correlated assets.
Analysis supports a long-term holding thesis rather than a trading strategy.

items.title: Major Investor Accumulation
points: Grant Cardone, a prominent real estate and business figure, acquired 60 BTC, adding to his existing holdings.
The purchase timing coincides with Morgan Stanley's research, suggesting a coordinated shift in investor sentiment.
